the regulation of hemoglobin affinity for O2 in acidosis and alkosis is achieved by the combined effects of 2, 3 DPG, red cell pH and MCHC.

the in vivo hemoglobins oxygen affinity of normal man is regulated by a combination of three mechanisms: 1. the direct pH (the Bohr) effect; 2. the change in red cell pH resulting from the change in 2,3 DPG; and 3. the direct change in hemoglobin affinity for O2 resulting from the change of red cell 2-3 DPG.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate content in the red blood cells is the main factor that regulates the oxygen-hemoglobin dissociation curve in vivo.
the 2,3-BPG effect on the hemoglobin-oxygen equilibrium curve is a function of pH.
the red cell 2-3-DPG content can be regulated to maintain hemoglobin oxygen affinity constant in vivo in response to changes in blood pH.
